yarn-dinkum.meaning: Every guideline survives, in order: "Cold tucker should be kept at 40 °F (4 °C) or below", "put a bit aside separately before the raw meat, poultry or seafood goes in", "Have a clean platter and utensils ready next to the barbie". The added "(4 °C)" is a helpful gloss, not a new claim.
yarn-dinkum.sense: Terms fit: "esky", "frozen ice bricks", "kitchen bench", "the perishables won't cop the warm air outside", "fruit and veg".
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Natural local vocabulary ("esky", "rocked up", "dead important", "bacteria breed like rabbits"), but some lines are mechanical: "Pack and Cart Your Tucker Safely".
yarn-dinkum.register: A clear Aussie layer over a guide ("gives foodborne bacteria a field day", "once you've rocked up"), but long stretches stay close to the source wording: "Using the same platter or utensils that held raw meat, poultry or seafood lets bacteria from the raw food's juices get onto the cooked food." A touch light for level 4.
yarn-dinkum.tone: Stays a friendly but serious safety guide: "Don't cross-contaminate. Make sure raw meat, poultry and seafood stay wrapped up tight."
yarn-dinkum.flow: Reads cleanly; the triple "running tap water" in one paragraph is carried over: "Rub the firm-skinned ones under running tap water, or give them a scrub with a clean vegie brush while you rinse them under running tap water."
yarn-dinkum.variety: "tucker" is leaned on throughout: "Keep cold tucker cold. Put cold tucker in an esky", "Keep “ready” tucker hot. Cooked tucker can be kept hot".
yarn-dinkum.essence: Recognisably the FDA picnic guide, headings and all: "Quick Tips for Setting Up at the Picnic Spot".

dinkum-3.meaning: All points kept: "Cold tucker needs to be kept at 40 °F (4 °C) or below", "If the packet says \"ready-to-eat,\" \"washed,\" or \"triple washed,\" you don't need to wash it", "Have a clean platter and utensils ready next to the barbie to serve up instead."
dinkum-3.sense: Mostly exact ("the tucker that goes off" for perishables, "Firm-skinned ones want a rub"), but "chook" narrows "poultry" to chicken, and "bacteria multiply quick smart" puts "quick smart" (promptly, on cue) where speed of growth is meant.
dinkum-3.authenticity: Sounds like an Australian explaining it: "Pop your cold tucker in an esky", "No running water handy?", "when everyone's in and out of the drinks esky topping up".
dinkum-3.register: Level-4 voice throughout a practical guide, no swearing (allowed): "Food safety starts with a proper clean of your mitts — outdoors as well."
dinkum-3.tone: Practical, mildly cautionary tone kept: "Trouble is, all that warm weather gives foodborne bacteria plenty of chances to thrive as well."
dinkum-3.flow: Smooth, but "the tucker that goes off" twice in two sentences is clunky: "packing the drinks in one esky and the tucker that goes off in another. That way, when everyone's in and out of the drinks esky topping up, the tucker that goes off isn't copping".
dinkum-3.variety: "tucker" and "mitts" are leaned on: "make sure your mitts and the surfaces are clean. Cleaning Your Mitts Outdoors".
dinkum-3.essence: Clearly the original guide, retold: "Keep the eskies shut: Once you're there, open the esky as few times as you can."

unharnessed.meaning: Points survive, with "tongs" narrowing utensils in one place: "Using the same platter or tongs that had raw meat, chook or seafood on them". "frozen gel packs" and the 40 °F threshold are kept.
unharnessed.sense: Several terms strain: "all that warm-weather carry-on" (carry-on is fuss or silly behaviour, not events), "gives the nasty bugs in your tucker a real chance to go off" (go off is food spoiling or a party), "washing your hands properly — out in the bush too" (a park picnic is not the bush).
unharnessed.authenticity: Plenty of real idiom ("cooked to buggery", "lugging your tucker", "copping a dose of food poisoning"), alongside forced lines like "gives the nasty bugs in your tucker a real chance to go off".
unharnessed.register: Level 4 with dad-level swears only: "bacteria breed like bloody rabbits", "stops it getting cooked to buggery".
unharnessed.tone: Mostly a safety guide still, though the swearing nudges it toward a laugh: "bacteria breed like bloody rabbits".
unharnessed.flow: Generally smooth, with a muddled opening: "But all that warm-weather carry-on also gives the nasty bugs in your tucker a real chance to go off."
unharnessed.variety: Varied: "lugging", "dishing it up", "Stick cold food", "wrapped up good and tight", "cooked to buggery", with "food" and "tucker" alternated.
unharnessed.essence: Still the picnic food-safety guide: "Keep the eskies shut: Once you're at the picnic spot, open the esky as little as you can."

yarn-troppo.meaning: Every guideline kept; additions hang off the original: "Don't reuse marinade. Once the raw stuff's been in it, that's it.", "Always use it to make sure your food's cooked right through. Don't go by looks.", "doesn't need washing, so don't bother."
yarn-troppo.sense: Each term fits: "Giving food a head start" for partial cooking, "the perishables aren't copping a blast of warm air every time the lid comes up", "Here's the drum".
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Reads like a local: "every man and his dog is in and out of the drinks esky for a top-up", "Chuck the cold stuff in an esky". "go together like a pie and sauce" is a touch stock.
yarn-troppo.register: Full level-4 voice on a guide, with one dad-level swear: "those little buggers breed like rabbits".
yarn-troppo.tone: Friendly but still a safety guide: "Make sure the raw meat, poultry and seafood stay wrapped up good and tight."
yarn-troppo.flow: Reads like it was written that way: "Once it's done, the tucker can be kept hot till it's served by shoving it over to the side of the grill rack, just away from the coals."
yarn-troppo.variety: Varied openers and terms: "Picture this", "Here's the drum", "Have a think", "every man and his dog", "head start", "pie and sauce".
yarn-troppo.essence: Unmistakably the guide retold, every heading kept: "Follow Safe Barbie Tips".

engine.meaning: The source with words swapped, so nothing is lost: "Cold tucker should be stored at 40 °F or below to prevent bacterial growth."
engine.sense: The swaps mostly fit ("esky", "kitchen bench", "fronted up"), but "tucker" lands in formal phrases that keep the source's sense only stiffly: "Cook tucker thoroughly".
engine.authenticity: Mechanical: slang dropped into US officialese, with US forms left in: "Organize esky contents. Consider packing beverages in one cooler and perishable tucker in another."
engine.register: Largely untranslated for a level-4 brief: "Food safety begins with proper hand cleaning — including in outdoor settings."
engine.tone: The original's tone is intact, since the wording is: "safe food handling when eating outdoors is critical".
engine.flow: Clunky where swaps clash with the formal frame: "Keep coolers closed: Once at the picnic site, limit the number of times the esky is opened".
engine.variety: One word does nearly all the work: "Grilled tucker can be kept hot", "serve your tucker", "Marinate tucker in the fridge".
engine.essence: The original guide, nearly verbatim: "Grilling and picnicking often go hand-in-hand."

yarn-dinkum.quote: Keep cold tucker cold. Put cold tucker in an esky
yarn-dinkum.original: Keep cold food cold. Place cold food in a cooler
yarn-dinkum.why: "tucker" swapped in for nearly every "food"; a reader notices the repetition.

yarn-dinkum.quote: Pack and Cart Your Tucker Safely
yarn-dinkum.why: "Cart" is an odd, un-Australian choice for transport.

dinkum-3.why: "chook" is chicken; poultry also covers turkey, duck and the rest.
"quick smart" means promptly, not fast growth; it strains here.

dinkum-3.quote: make sure your mitts and the surfaces are clean. Cleaning Your Mitts Outdoors
dinkum-3.original: make sure hands and surfaces are clean. Outdoor Hand Cleaning

unharnessed.quote: all that warm-weather carry-on also gives the nasty bugs in your tucker a real chance to go off
unharnessed.original: these warm weather events also present opportunities for foodborne bacteria to thrive
unharnessed.why: "carry-on" means fuss; "go off" means spoil or party. Both take the wrong sense.
The bush is not just "outdoors"; it changes the setting.

unharnessed.quote: Using the same platter or tongs
unharnessed.original: Using the same platter or utensils

yarn-troppo.quote: Picnics and a cook-up on the barbie go together like a pie and sauce.
yarn-troppo.original: Grilling and picnicking often go hand-in-hand.
yarn-troppo.why: A slightly stock simile, though natural enough.

engine.quote: Organize esky contents. Consider packing beverages in one cooler
engine.original: Organize cooler contents. Consider packing beverages in one cooler
engine.why: US spelling left in, and "esky" and "cooler" mixed in one line.
"tucker" substituted mechanically throughout an otherwise untranslated text.

summaries.yarn-dinkum: Faithful and natural, slightly light for level 4, with "tucker" overused.
summaries.dinkum-3: Natural, well-pitched level-4 guide; small sense stretches and some leaned-on words.
summaries.unharnessed: Colourful and varied but strains several terms in the opening and setting.
summaries.yarn-troppo: The most natural and varied level-4 retelling; faithful, with colour that hangs off the original.
summaries.engine: A word-swap pass: "tucker" and "esky" dropped into the original, far lighter than level 4.
